parsed.title: Turn contract still requires Product-review gate on replan route
parsed.detail: The turn contract box reads unconditionally: "Then the Product-review gate ran: no current `spec-review-pass` receipt bound to the recomputed snapshot → STOP with its fixed block". ROUTING.md's new replan exemption says a `route: replan` line means "skip the STOP and load the replan contract". A unit with an open replan finding has by definition just had its plan invalidated, so no current spec-review-pass receipt exists — the turn contract would force the STOP the exemption forbids. The contract was not updated to carve out the replan route.

parsed.title: "Both resources" stale after allowlist grew to four
parsed.detail: The same hunk rewrites the progressive-loading list from two entries to four (adding planning-preflight consumption and the replan contract), yet the following unchanged sentence still reads "Do not load planning gates after a redirect stop. Both resources are normative, one hop from this file" — 'Both' no longer matches the list it governs.

parsed.title: Replan exemption contradicts the done-state 'never a replan' guard
parsed.detail: The exemption says "A `route: replan` line means ... skip the STOP" with no state restriction, but step 4 of the same file states for roadmap status `done`: "replanning stays forbidden — the feature is fully built" and its STOP block ends "no PR is open → the row is mislabeled or execution stopped → /execute-phase <NN> (never a replan)". A done unit with an open finding whose frozen route is plan-owner would print `route: replan` and, per the exemption, bypass the STOP the file declares absolute.

parsed.title: Replan contract loaded as step 7, after drafting and hand-off
parsed.detail: Allowlist item 7 ("Only when `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <N>` prints `route: replan` ... load the replan contract ... instead of a new fix SPEC") is numbered after item 6, the review-plan hand-off step. PLANNING_PROCESS.md mandates the opposite order: "run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` first ... do not draft a new fix SPEC" — before ingest (step 1). Following the SKILL's numbered order, the new fix SPEC and ledgers are already drafted before the replan contract loads.

parsed.title: Freeze-batch routes decision-required rows to a replan planner
parsed.detail: The freeze-batch condition is "any row whose frozen class is `replan-in-unit` or `decision-required`" and the new Next routes to `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` "whose `route: replan` line names the planner that re-cuts the plan". But CLASSIFY.md defines `decision-required` as "a new product/architecture decision is unavoidable. Stop and surface it; the unit blocks until the user decides" — no plan is re-cut. For a batch containing only a decision-required row, the docs promise the router prints `route: replan` and names a planner, contradicting the class's own blocking contract.

parsed.title: Fixed verdict block not updated for the router step
parsed.detail: The prose now says a `replan-in-unit` correction means "Run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`", but the fixed per-finding output block still reads "Action taken: <current-unit fold/phase | plan-feature | plan-fix | user decision>" — the router run (the newly mandated action) has no slot in the fixed format, and the block still names the planners directly as actions.

parsed.title: Sensor duplicates the router's class→destination decision
parsed.detail: Step 13 is declared the "single-sourced trigger surface", and the new entry itself admits "the same class→destination decision `scripts/unit-route.mjs` owns" — yet it hardcodes `{command: "/plan-feature <unit>" | "/plan-fix <issue>", ...}` in the sensor instead of delegating to the router, re-deriving in a second place the very decision unit 224 centralizes. It also emits the planner directly, so the `route: replan` gate the rest of the unit makes mandatory is never run on this path.

parsed.title: Closing block asserts the router prints replan unconditionally
parsed.detail: The rewritten line: "any finding routed replan-in-unit or owned by plan? → `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` prints `route: replan` and names the planner". It states the router's output as a guaranteed fact for any plan-owned finding, but the router's route is derived from the ledger's frozen rows; a plan-owned finding that is not carried as a `replan-in-unit` row (e.g. persisted before this feature, or classified otherwise) need not produce `route: replan`, and the instruction gives no fallback for any other router output.
